Space-time scan statistic of incidents

Source: R/kscan.R
kscan.Rd

Kulldorff's space-time permutation scan (Kulldorff, Heffernan, Hartman, Assuncao and Mostashari 2005), which needs the incidents alone, no population: cylinders are circles of radius r about each distinct incident location times windows [s, s + tw) that start at each distinct incident time. A cylinder holding c incidents, of n_C in its circle (at any time) and n_W in its window (anywhere), expects e = n_C n_W / n when place and time are independent, and scores the Poisson log-likelihood ratio c log(c / e) + (n - c) log((n - c) / (n - e)) when c > e, 0 otherwise (Kulldorff 1997). The most likely cluster has the largest ratio; secondary clusters follow in order of their ratio, each the best of its circle among those whose circles overlap none chosen before. Each p-value compares the cluster's ratio with the largest ratio of the whole scan with the times shuffled among the locations nsim times from seed, so a secondary cluster's p-value is conservative. That the ratio is never negative is proved in Lean: see proof("kscan"). The work grows as the number of locations times length(r) times the distinct times times length(tw), for the scan and for each permutation.

Usage

kscan(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  t,
  r,
  tw,
  minc = 2,
  top = 1,
  nsim = 999,
  seed = NULL,
  lonlat = FALSE
)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

t

The times: numbers (days, say), or Date or POSIXct (taken in days), one per incident.

r

The radii of the circles: positive and increasing, in the unit of the coordinates (metres when lonlat = TRUE).

tw

The lengths of the windows: positive, in the unit of t.

minc

The fewest incidents a cluster holds: a whole number from 1.

top

The most clusters reported: a whole number from 1.

nsim

The number of permutations: a whole number from 0.

seed

NULL to draw the simulations' seed from R's generator (so set.seed() fixes them), or one whole number from 0.

lonlat

FALSE (the default) when x and y are planar coordinates in one length unit; TRUE when they are longitude and latitude in degrees, which are then projected to metres by eqproj() about their own centre, and centres are returned in degrees. It is never guessed.

Value

A list of class kscan: cl, a data frame with one row per cluster, most likely first: its centre x, y (in degrees when lonlat = TRUE), r, start and end (the window [start, end)), n (incidents in the cylinder), exp, ncirc and nwin (incidents in its circle and in its window), rr (the relative risk inside against outside), llr and p ((1 + #{max* >= llr}) / (nsim + 1), NaN without permutations); memb, each incident's cluster or NA; n and nsim.

References

Kulldorff, M. (1997). A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 26(6), 1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995

Kulldorff, M., Heffernan, R., Hartman, J., Assuncao, R. and Mostashari, F. (2005). A space-time permutation scan statistic for disease outbreak detection. PLoS Medicine, 2(3), e59. doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.0020059

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = c(runif(150, 0, 20), rnorm(20, 5, 0.3)),
           y = c(runif(150, 0, 20), rnorm(20, 15, 0.3)))
t <- c(sample(0:99, 150, TRUE), sample(40:44, 20, TRUE))
s <- kscan(p, t = t, r = c(1, 3), tw = c(5, 20), top = 2, nsim = 99,
           seed = 1)
s
#> kscan: 2 clusters of 170 incidents, 99 permutations
#>         x        y r start end  n       exp ncirc nwin        rr       llr    p
#>  4.959446 15.23629 1    40  45 20 3.4117647    20   29  6.510345 19.636580 0.01
#>  9.544601 11.09801 3     4   9  4 0.3235294    11    5 12.637459  6.422689 0.12
